name: Deadeye Shore
summary: Deadeye Shore is a windswept stretch of coastline along Durotar's eastern edge, directly east of Drygulch Ravine. Named in memory of the legendary Bleeding Hollow chieftain Kilrogg Deadeye, the barren sands are roamed primarily by wild raptors, scorpids, and feral boars.

sections.title: A Shoreline of the Bleeding Hollow
sections.body: Stretching beneath the red bluffs of central Durotar, Deadeye Shore takes its name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow clan who fought in the First and Second Wars. From high above, the sand and rocky outcrops faintly mirror the shape of a skull with a missing eye socket. While lacking major settlements or military outposts, the shoreline is far from peaceful: aggressive wildlife dominates the sands, and shadowy cultists from the Burning Blade have been known to prowl down toward the water from their nearby hideouts in the ravines.

faq.q: Why is it called Deadeye Shore?
faq.answer: The shoreline is named after Kilrogg Deadeye, the famed chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow clan. The natural coastal terrain also resembles a skull missing an eye, echoing the chieftain's own blinded socket.

No permanent settlements stand on Deadeye Shore. The stretch of coast is inhabited primarily by native wildlife like raptors, scorpids, and boars, though fishermen and travelers occasionally pass through—sometimes running afoul of hidden Burning Blade cultists.

faq.q: What threats are found around Deadeye Shore?
faq.answer: Beyond aggressive local beasts, the greatest danger comes from the neighboring Drygulch Ravine. Cultists belonging to the Burning Blade occasionally wander down from the rocky canyons toward the coast, ambushing unwary travelers and fishermen.

angles.text: For orcs establishing their new nation in Durotar, the shore honors Kilrogg Deadeye, reminding them of the old chieftains who shaped the Horde's history during the wars on Azeroth.
